bib.title: Scaling Behavior of Single LLM-Driven Multi-Agent Systems

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Scaling Behavior of Single LLM-Driven Multi-Agent Systems", Jialing Li, Zhouhong Gu, Yin Cai, Hongwei Feng (Fudan University). arXiv:2606.00655v1 [cs.MA], 30 May 2026. Preprint; the text I read shows no venue. The formatting looks like an ACL-style submission.

COVERAGE: Read 82,595 of 82,595 chars. I read the main text, limitations, appendices A to E and the references. I skimmed the tail, which is the Table 5/6 dataset examples. Figures are images, so I did not read plotted values, only the text and captions. The only numbers I quote are from the text.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Claim: With one base LLM, accuracy rises, peaks at an optimal agent count n*, then falls (inverted U). It does not rise monotonically. This holds if the system is "sufficiently driven" (at least two n >= 2 match or beat the single agent).
  number: n varied 1 to 8; token cost is quadratic in n.
  setup: SIMAS (sequential chain, 3 rounds, same-model agents with distinct personality/belief/expertise profiles). Llama-3.1 8B/70B and Qwen2.5 7B/72B. MMLU, 6 subjects, 17 questions each, 3 repeats averaged. Small samples.
  quote: "If a MAS is sufficiently driven, the performance will scale with diminishing returns, following an inverted-U relationship with agent count." Also: "within SIMAS, token cost scales quadratically with n (Figure 3)."
  where: Sec 4.2, p5-6.
- Claim: Small models (7B/8B) never benefit. They degrade monotonically as agents are added, so a capability threshold exists.
  number: none
  setup: Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-7B versus 70B/72B, MMLU subjects.
  quote: "smaller models (7B/8B parameters) proved fundamentally inadequate for multi-agent collaboration, showing monotonic performance degradation with additional agents, suggesting a minimum capability threshold"
  where: App D.2, p13.
- Claim: Task type sets the best n. Logic and maths chains collapse as agents are added. Fact and interpretive tasks tolerate more agents, and Llama on Philosophy shows a U-shaped recovery. The authors call that recovery "pseudo-stability" (majority-consensus noise suppression), not real collaboration.
  number: Formal logic 58.82% (n=1) to 25.49% (n=8); abstract algebra 52.94% to 25.49%; the main text gives a 27.45% drop for Llama-3.1-70B.
  setup: Llama-3.1-70B, MMLU. Single-agent baseline is n=1.
  quote: "for formal logic, accuracy declined substantially from 58.82% (1 agent) to 25.49% (8 agents), a drop of 33.33 percentage points." Also: "accuracy drops substantially with more agents (27.45% from n=1 to n=8 for Llama-3.1-70B)".
  where: Sec 4.2 (p6), App D.3 (p13). Note the inconsistency: 27.45 in the main text versus 33.33 and 27.45 (52.94 to 25.49) in the appendix. The main text's 27.45 matches the abstract-algebra drop.
- Claim: The decline is caused by coordination overhead, not long context. Padding the history to a fixed length still gives the inverted U.
  number: Abstract Algebra 60.78% (n=2) to peak 72.55% (n=4), then 64.71% (n=8). Philosophy peaks at 98.04% (n=4,6).
  setup: Qwen2.5-72B, three MMLU subjects, neutral filler tokens fix total input length.
  quote: "Abstract Algebra rises from 60.78% (n=2) to a peak of 72.55% (n=4) before declining to 64.71% (n=8)"
  where: Sec 4.3, p7.
- Claim: A different topology (AutoGen GroupChat, fully connected, dynamic speaker selection) raises the peak a little and delays the decline. It does not remove the inverted U.
  number: 75.00% on Abstract Algebra (n=4,5); 70.59% on College Physics (n=5); Abstract Algebra falls to 50.00% at n=6; Philosophy falls from 94.12% (n=2) to 86.67% (n=8).
  setup: Llama3.1-70B only, same MMLU subjects.
  quote: "Abstract Algebra collapses to 50.00% at n=6, and Philosophy declines monotonically from 94.12% (n=2) to 86.67% (n=8). AutoGen runs exhibited substantially lower variance than SIMAS"
  where: Sec 4.4, p7.
- Claim: Naive SIMAS loses to single-agent CoT on reasoning. On AIME 2025 it "fails catastrophically" (figure only, no number in the text). The cause is fragmentation of the reasoning chain across turns, with unnoticed errors and drift. Coding and open-ended results are mixed and model-dependent.
  number: none in the text for AIME 2025.
  setup: Llama-3.1-70B and Qwen2.5-72B. Coding is 5 complex projects plus 15 open-ended questions, judged by an LLM agent, so judge bias is possible. Small custom sets.
  quote: "This failure mode stems from the fragmentation of coherent reasoning chains across sequential agent turns: without a dedicated mechanism to synthesize fragments into a unified line of reasoning or to correct accumulating errors, the collective output becomes disjointed"
  where: Sec 5, p8; case studies App E.4 (a polynomial over Z5 where an arithmetic slip went unchecked and the group answered wrongly) and E.5 (a "Two Sum" coding task where the group converged early, then spent a redundant round on irrelevant edge cases).
- Claim: Structured multi-agent designs (AutoGen, Multi-Agent Debate) with critique loops can beat single-agent CoT on hard maths. The benefit comes from the interaction design, not from agent count. ReAct is much worse.
  number: AIME 2024, Llama-3.1-70B: Naive-CoT 16.7, AutoGen 20.0, Debate 20.0, ReAct 0.0. GSM8K, Llama-3.1-70B: CoT 87.33, Debate 90.82, AutoGen 85.21, ReAct 20.09. Qwen2.5-72B GSM8K: CoT 75.13, AutoGen 81.80, Debate 75.81, ReAct 52.76.
  setup: Table 2 data is cited from Gu et al. 2025 (AgentGroupChat-V2), not the authors' own runs. Single runs, tiny AIME sample (30 problems; implied by the 3.3 steps).
  quote: "frameworks like AutoGen (Wu et al., 2023) and Multi-Agent Debate (Liang et al., 2023) incorporating structured workflows and critical evaluation loops surpass single-agent CoT on challenging benchmarks (e.g., AIME 2024: 16.7–20.0% vs. 16.7% Naive-CoT with Llama-3.1-70B)"
  where: Sec 5, Table 2, p8. The "16.7–20.0%" range includes a tie with the baseline, so it is weak evidence.
- Claim: Instability rises with n, then shows false stability at large n because the system fails consistently.
  number: Llama-3.1-70B std dev up to 17.32%.
  quote: "Llama-3.1-70B showed significant volatility despite its parameter advantage, with standard deviations reaching 17.32%"
  where: Finding 3, p7; App D.2.
- Claim: Model family changes n*. For Qwen2.5-72B the peak is at n=2 versus n=4 for Llama-3.1-70B, with College Physics peak accuracy of 86.27% versus 60.78%.
  quote: "optimal at 2 agents for Qwen2.5-72B versus 4 agents for Llama-3.1-70B ... (86.27% peak versus 60.78% for Llama-3.1)"
  where: App D.4, p15.
- Claim: Profile attributes (personality, beliefs, expertise) shift accuracy and stability but not the inverted-U shape.
  quote: "The scaling pattern ... remains consistent regardless of agent setting modifications."
  where: App D.5. Swings are large and discipline-specific; for example, removing beliefs costs up to -23.79 points in philosophy for Qwen.

LIMITS
- Conceded by the authors: only homogeneous agents on a single LLM; SIMAS has no voting or dynamic workflows; no DAG or hierarchical topologies tested; accuracy is the only metric; closed-book QA only; only up to 8 agents; no models above 70B.
- Not shown: heterogeneous models, tools, long-horizon tasks, or any reasoning-model baseline (all models are 2024-era open instruct models, so this may have dated).
- Small samples: 17 questions per subject (so each step is about 5.9 points), 3 repeats, and an LLM judge for generation tasks.
- AutoGen was tested on Llama-70B only. Table 2 is borrowed from a prior paper.
- "Quadratic token cost" is stated with a pointer to Figure 3. No derivation is given in the text.
- The abstract's "scaling law" framing is stronger than the evidence, which shows qualitative shapes with noisy peaks.
- The text says the setup "aligns with the practical band of deployed MAS like AutoGen". That is an assertion.

BUILDS ON
- AutoGen (Wu et al., 2023, arXiv); CAMEL (Li et al., 2023); MetaGPT (Hong et al., 2023); AgentVerse (Chen et al., 2023); ChatDev (Qian et al., 2023); Multi-Agent Debate (Liang et al., 2023).
- Qian et al., 2025, MacNet, ICLR: DAG topology, logistic growth to hundreds or thousands of agents. Contrasting concurrent work.
- Cemri et al., 2025, "Why do Multi-Agent LLM systems fail?" (arXiv:2503.13657); Flint et al., 2025 (group size effects, arXiv:2510.22422); Shehata and Li, 2026 (bystander effect, arXiv:2605.10698); Gu et al., 2025 (AgentGroupChat-V2, arXiv:2506.15451, source of Table 2).
- Chain-of-Thought (Wei et al., 2022, NeurIPS); Toolformer; Chain of Agents (Zhang et al., ICLR 2025); benchmarks MMLU (Hendrycks et al., ICLR 2021), E-KAR (Luo et al., ACL 2022), AIME.

CODE: Algorithm 1 (p4) in prose. Initialize h0={q}. For each round t in 1..T and each agent a_i in order: r = Pi(h_{i-1,t}, a_i); h_i = h_{i-1} U {r}. Return Pi(h_{n,T}, a_1), so the first agent synthesizes the final answer. Default T=3. Profile triple = (personality in {FRIENDLY, SKEPTICAL, NEUTRAL, AGGRESSIVE}, beliefs, expertise), LLM-generated, with the last agent forced AGGRESSIVE (Fig 10 prompt, p12).

FIGURES: Best candidate is Figure 7 (p7), "Llama3.1-70B under AutoGen debate. The inverted-U pattern persists under AutoGen's structured debate topology." It shows that the inverted U holds beyond the chain topology, which is what the topology-patterns note needs. Alternative: Figure 1 (p2), the SIMAS workflow. I did not run the figures script, and I did not view the figure images.

PROBLEMS: Extraction was clean. No embedded instructions. Figure content is not in the text. Minor typos in the source (e.g. "assistent"). The 27.45 vs 33.33 figures in the task-type claim are inconsistent between main text and appendix, as noted above. The reference list has some garbled author names (e.g. Qian 2023 ChatDev, Xi 2023), so I would not copy author lists from it.

Fit to notes: this is chain/fully-connected topology evidence for 05-topology-patterns.md. It suits 06-when-not-to-build-a-graph.md for two points: more agents is not better, and a well-prompted single CoT agent can win on reasoning tasks. It is evidence about same-model homogeneous agents only. Do not generalise it to graph or DAG topologies, which it did not test.
